transcript.note: Round 1 (retry after two rejections taught me two constraints the export doesn't spell out: (a) a moved vertex may never cross past a neighbour's row/column, it can only approach it -- this killed my first attempt to swap vertices 15 and 3 past each other; (b) the grid's real bounds are cols=8/rows=11 even though vertices 1, 2, 10, 12 already sit outside that range, so targets must land inside [0,7]x[0,10] even for those). Revised plan, hub vertex 8 (row-locked r4 via two H segs) slides its free column from 3 to 4 to meet vertex 3's column, verticaling 8-3 -- sacrificing 8-7's existing 45-degree diagonal since 7 is fully double-locked and can't follow, and 8 is now double-locked too so nothing else can save it. Vertex 5 (free column, row-locked r8) also slides to column 4, verticaling 5-3 since 3 didn't move. Vertex 6 (row-locked r2) slides its free column from 3 to 2 to meet vertex 11's column (2), verticaling 11-6; the cell was nominally occupied by vertex 16 in the export dump but 16 has zero segments so it never entered the alignment graph and isn't a real collision. Free termini 1 and 2 (degree-1, unconstrained except by their one neighbour) slide onto neighbour 9's column and neighbour 7's row respectively, while also pulling into grid bounds, verticaling 1-9 and horizontaling 7-2. Net: 5 of 6 previously off-axis segments become exact H/V; only 8-7 is sacrificed, which is unavoidable given both its endpoints are fully locked elsewhere.
